description: dsh hook-bridge guide corrected: one project-neutral mount, and the interpreter probe that cannot run under DSH's confined sandbox
changelog:
**Corrected — the DSH hook-bridge mount is one per machine, not one per project.** `.dsh/DSH.md` told operators to point `configPath` at their own project and set `projectDir`, and claimed a second DSH project needs its own mount. The generated hook commands are project-relative and the bridge runs them with `cwd` set to the session workspace, so one `configPath` already serves every Trellis project: mount a `$DSH_HOME` copy of any project's `.dsh/hooks.json` and each session executes its own project's scripts. `projectDir` is now deliberately omitted — it only sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and defaults per run to the session workspace, whereas setting it pinned every project's hooks to one project's directory.

**Corrected — pinning `TRELLIS_PYTHON` does not fix the Windows hook failure.** `run-python-hook.cjs` chooses an interpreter by probing each candidate with captured (piped) output. DSH runs hook commands through its shell service, which the file sandbox confines, so under `workspace-write` (the default) or `read-only` the piped spawn is refused, every candidate looks unusable, and the hook exits 127 before Python ever runs. A pinned `TRELLIS_PYTHON` is probed the same way, so it cannot help. `.dsh/DSH.md` now documents the two options that do work: name the interpreter directly in the mounted config (`<absolute python.exe> -X utf8 .dsh/hooks/<script>.py`, which runs no probe), or run DSH unconfined (`DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access`). The Windows example no longer names one contributor's Conda environment.

Documentation only — no project file, hook script, or generated config changes.
notes: No `--migrate` required. Downstream projects pick the corrected `.dsh/DSH.md` up on their next `trellis update`; the version bump is what surfaces the update-available nudge beforehand. Nothing in `.dsh/hooks.json`, the hook scripts, or any other platform's generated files changed. A project that already mounted the bridge per the old instructions keeps working — it is simply limited to the one project its `configPath` names until it is repointed at a shared copy.
